## Original problem

I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

{"body": "The exposed material now has three contributions and a carry that reads them, and the carry's central move is one I want to keep and then narrow. The account proposed a written list and committed itself to the claim that a specification-ambiguity is doing real explanatory work. The objection committed itself to a behavioral difference between specification ambiguity and performance disagreement, and to a diagnostic first step asked separately and in writing. The carry takes up the rival's diagnostic step but revises the question from an open characterization to a concrete instance, demotes the written list from load-bearing to incidental, and declines to answer the original question with a procedure at all.

I think the carry's most defensible claim is the one about the trigger, and I want to separate it from the frame it was offered in. The carry says a procedure that depends on its own trigger is a weak procedure, because the person most likely to raise the issue is the person not avoiding. That is not the same as the account's concession that the procedure assumes two flatmates willing to engage. The concession says the proposal has a precondition. The trigger point says the precondition is not just a gate at the entrance; it is the same disposition the procedure is supposed to work on, so the procedure can only reach the cases where it was not needed. The carry flags this as possibly a restatement of the account's own concession and says it does not know how to settle that. I think it is a distinct point, and the reason is that a precondition can be met without being met by the procedure, whereas a trigger that selects for the non-avoiding party means the procedure's access set is defined by the outcome it is meant to produce. If that reading is wrong — if the account's concession already amounts to this — then the point is redundant and should be absorbed rather than pressed.

On the concrete-instance revision: I would take it up, but I want to be clear about what it buys and what it does not. The carry argues that fixing the referent makes the answer less selectable than an open characterization question. The objection's own commitments include the worry that the asker's report is a compression and may not have the diagnostic weight given to it. The concrete-instance move does not address that worry about the asker; it only addresses selection in the two respondents. So the revision is a partial fix at best, and the three-way distinction the material cannot make is still not made. I would keep the move, and I would stop describing it as giving purchase on the three-way distinction. What it gives is a shared referent across three answers, which is a different and smaller thing.

On the written list: I agree with the carry that making a disagreement legible is not resolving it, and I agree with the objection that this is a cost rather than only a gain. But I want to resist the demotion being read as a free move. If the list is non-load-bearing, then the account's structural-ambiguity claim no longer has to answer to whether the list works, and the carry itself notes this weakens falsifiability. I would rather state the trade directly: the list survives as an artifact people can point to, at the price of no longer serving as a test of the diagnosis it was introduced to serve. That is a real loss, and it is the kind of loss I would want a later reader to see rather than a demotion presented as prudence.

On what to say to the asker: the carry would ask whether the other two flatmates think there is a problem at all. I would keep that, and I would not phrase it as a procedure. The danger the carry names — that the question can be heard as an accusation — is real, and I do not have a phrasing that removes it. I would also note that this question, asked by one flatmate, is itself the intervention the carry says a circulated re-framing is. So the carry's own preferred first move is already inside the thing being diagnosed, not a neutral step before it, and I do not think the material supports anything more conclusive than that.", "commitments": "Taking this up commits me to a reading of the trigger point as distinct from the account's concession about willingness, and to the further claim that a procedure whose access set is defined by the disposition it aims to change is weaker than one whose precondition is merely a gate. I have no evidence that this distinction makes an operational difference in a three-person flat; it may be a distinction without a consequence, and if the account's concession already covers it, the point should be dropped rather than pressed as new.

It commits me to the concrete-instance question as a partial rather than a general improvement. I am not claiming it addresses the worry about the asker's report as a compression; that worry remains, and the objection's commitments already carry it. If a later reader uses the concrete-instance move to say the three-way distinction is now diagnosable, that use is beyond what I am prepared to support.

It commits me to a specific framing of the demotion: the written list survives as an artifact at the cost of its role as a test. I am proposing that this be stated as a loss rather than presented as a neutral demotion, and I am aware that the framing is itself contestable — someone could argue the list was never a test and so nothing was lost.

There are dependencies I cannot discharge. The claim that the asker's question to the other flatmates is itself an intervention presupposes that the asker is one of the three; the material does not establish this and the carry already flags it. My reading of the trigger point presupposes that the procedure is triggered by a flatmate raising the issue rather than by a scheduled review; if the procedure is scheduled, the trigger argument does not apply.

What is unresolved on my side: whether the trigger point is a criticism of the account or a restatement of the account's own concession, and I do not currently know how to settle that; whether the concrete-instance revision changes the diagnostic yield at all or only changes the style of the answer; and whether a list that is no longer load-bearing can still be useful enough to keep, given that its usefulness and its testability may have been the same property. I would not want a later reader to treat the concrete-instance move as validated, or the demotion as costless, or the trigger point as newly established."}

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
